variants.headline: Ordered goods reach the dock
variants.sub: Imported {good} ordered by {company} has landed at the colony's port.
variants.body:
The company {company} has received {qty} units of {good} at the port. The order arrived a full round trip after it was placed and was paid for on the dock. For {target}, the event is a practical test of the connection between ordering, waiting and obtaining goods.

People live through the interval between an order and its arrival. Labour should keep that ordinary perspective in view when discussing imports. Goods matter through the lives they serve; a completed delivery deserves attention without making the person who needs provision disappear behind the commercial account.

The handling of {target} merits scrutiny through the completed delivery. The order has landed and been paid for; the long interval is part of the practical record, not a detail to overlook. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.

variants.headline: An order completes its long journey
variants.sub: The company {company} has taken delivery of its home-world order of {good}.
variants.body:

variants.body:
